proposals.title: Build a Customer-Reply Draft That Waits for Your Approval (n8n, Beginner)
proposals.hook: A new lead arrives, the reply is already written, and nothing is sent until you read it.
proposals.summary: A contact-form lead goes into n8n, gets checked, and comes back as a drafted reply in a plain text file with sent: false. The owner reads it and sends it from their own email. Built with made-up data only.
outline: The one rule: draft, never send, and why an automation that can send can also send the wrong text a hundred times
The flow: Webhook, Validate & draft, Input valid?, append the lead to a file, respond with the draft
Test it with a made-up lead on the Test URL (one call per click)
Send a bad lead with no phone: a 400 with the list of problems, and no row written
Read the draft in Leads.md and change the placeholders to your own words
The approval step: you read it and send it yourself; there is no send node
Recap, and where the full pack goes further

demo.description: The sample inquiry, the draft and the deliberate review step, on a local n8n.
demo.input: {"name":"Dana Reyes","email":"dana@example.com","phone":"+1 (555) 010-2233","message":"Need a quote for a kitchen faucet repair"}
demo.expected_output: {"status":"draft","sent":false,...,"next":"owner approves before anything is sent"}, and one new row in inbox/Leads.md
demo.bad_expected_output: {"error":"invalid input","details":["phone is required"],"sent":false,...} and no new row
demo.source: Products/Local Business Automation Pack/guide/Chapter 4 - Workflow 2, Lead form to drafted reply.md; VERIFY-LOG.md (1 Oct 2026, n8n 2.40.7)

proposals.title: Organize Client Notes with Claude + Obsidian: From a Messy Note to a Weekly Review
proposals.hook: A rough note from a client call becomes a clean client note, with the client's own words kept and the gaps listed.
proposals.summary: Open a folder as an Obsidian vault, give Claude house rules in a CLAUDE.md, and turn a made-up conversation note into a client note and a weekly review that only uses numbers you can check.
outline: Open a folder as a vault in Obsidian, and run Claude Code in the same folder
House rules in CLAUDE.md: keep the client's words, mark summaries, never invent a number, draft rather than send
Paste a made-up conversation note and ask Claude to fill a client note from the template
Check the result: the client's own words in their own section, blanks left blank, gaps listed
Link a project note to the client
A weekly review where money lines hold only numbers you can check
Sorting the inbox: Claude shows the plan and waits for your yes

proposals.title: Test Your n8n Workflow Before It Touches Real Customer Data
proposals.hook: Three made-up inputs show whether a workflow is ready: a good one, a bad one and a hostile one.
proposals.summary: How to test an n8n workflow with made-up data before real customers reach it: Test URL versus Production URL, good and bad inputs, a hostile input that must be escaped, and reading the Executions tab when something fails.
outline: Made-up data only: example.com addresses and 555 phone numbers
Test URL versus Production URL, and why a test webhook answers one call per click
A good input and the output you expect
A bad input: the workflow should refuse it with a 400 and write nothing
A hostile input: HTML, a link and table characters, escaped in the file
When a run fails: Executions, the red node, Debug in editor
A quiet failure: success, but the wrong answer
Only then publish, and watch the first real runs

demo.description: Sample inputs, the expected output and the failure handling, on a local n8n.
demo.input: A lead named "Eve | Mallory" whose message is [[Secret note]] **bold**
demo.expected_output: HTTP 200, and the row shows Eve \| Mallory and the message escaped (<img ...> \[\[Secret note\]\] \*\*bold\*\*)
demo.bad_expected_output: HTTP 400 with ["from must be an E.164 number, e.g. +15551234567"] and no row written
demo.quiet_failure: An If condition that reads {{ $json.minute }} instead of minutes: status success, wrong advice
demo.source: Products/Local Business Automation Pack/VERIFY-LOG.md (1 Oct 2026); guide/Chapter 8 - When something goes wrong.md; Products/AI for Every Age/adults/Lesson 7.10 - Fixing problems with Executions.md

proposals.next_step: The pack ships four workflows already tested this way, with the test calls, what came back, and a chapter on the six usual problems.
cautions: Never paste a real customer's details, an inbox file or a key into a forum post or an AI tool when asking for help; the guide says the same.
Execution records can hold whatever passed through the workflow: test with made-up data.

proposals.title: Practise a Family Callback Rule for Suspicious Calls (A Calm Drill)
proposals.hook: One rule your family can practise at the kitchen table: stop, hang up, and call back on a number you already know.
proposals.summary: A calm household exercise with clearly fictional names: the callback rule, the four steps, and one announced practice call. A plan made ahead of time, not a promise that it stops every scam.
outline: The rule: if a call or message asks for money, a code or personal details, stop, hang up, and call back on a number you already know
Why caller ID isn't proof, in the FTC's words
The four steps, and what you should see after each
Ground rules for practice: always announced, "This is a drill", made-up names, never your real safe word
Drill 1 with fictional names: ask for the family word, "I'll call you right back", hang up, say who you'd call
Long-distance families: arrange the practice call first, and ring back as yourself
One thing to do today: save your bank's number from the back of your card

demo.description: Walk through a calm household exercise using clearly fictional examples.
demo.input: Caller reads: "This is a drill. ... Grandma? It's me. I've had an accident and I'm in real trouble. I need you to send money today. Please don't tell Mom and Dad."
demo.expected_output: The answerer asks "What's our word?", says "I'll call you right back", puts the phone down, and says out loud who they would call and where the number is.
demo.source: Products/Family AI-Scam Defense Workbook/workbook/Part 3 - The callback rule.md; Part 7 - Family drills.md; VERIFY-LOG.md (FTC and FBI pages read 5 Oct 2026)
